accuracy.reason: Precise authority, cache-aside actors, key identity, stale-refill race, TTL versus source age, eviction and outage qualifications; no false freshness or fallback guarantees.

evidence.quote: Invalidation alone does not guarantee freshness. To avoid charging an old price at checkout, validate the price against the authoritative data as part of accepting the order.

mechanisms.reason: Hit/miss diagrams and interleaved old-fill example expose state and causality. Local/shared failure scope and coalescing/admission behavior let learners trace both normal and failure paths.

evidence.quote: Falling back to the database is a load decision, not a free recovery path.

coherence.reason: All eight card objectives build reuse, hit/miss, keys, invalidation, removal, topology and overload into an integrated cache-or-not decision. Prerequisites suffice.

evidence.quote: Name the cached result, its key, acceptable staleness, update policy, and failure behavior.

decisions.reason: Cost/reuse/freshness determine whether to cache; currency/private-key examples, authoritative checkout, shared-copy tradeoff and bounded fallback make choices actionable.

evidence.quote: Define what the key identifies, who fills it, and where the authoritative data lives.

clarity.reason: Plain definitions and short examples isolate each distinction; the learner transfers to six different workloads without relying on extra protocols.

evidence.quote: TTL limits an entry's lifetime, not the age of the source data used to fill it.

outcomes.reason: Uses station plus language key and relates repeated 80ms work to 2ms hits; identifies API as reader/filler, distinguishes hit/miss and source authority, and accounts for lookup/fill/storage maintenance costs.
Correctly traces old hours refilled after deletion and rejects unconditional post-write freshness; bypass to authoritative database follows the explicit commit-visibility prerequisite.
Correct hit/miss times for both cases, distinguishes TTL expiration from early capacity eviction, and rejects automatic refresh, guaranteed residence or source-age guarantee.

Selects shared entry under no-concurrent-fill assumptions; explains other local copies remain old, local versus network lookup, independent loss versus all-instance shared loss and lack of automatic freshness. Makes no unsupported application-failure inference.

Explains duplicate source work during expiration and one-in-progress coalesced fetch; caps aggregate outage fallback against 500 reads/s, rejects excess and treats stale independently retained data as optional and bounded, never readable from unreachable cache.
Rejects cache because no second read benefits, cites ample latency/capacity headroom, identifies fill/storage costs and relevant repeated/expensive-work trigger with staleness constraints.

sourceChecks.claim: Azure caching guidance confirms repeated expensive reads and costs of keeping copies; source-of-truth database is an explicit scope choice consistent with cache-aside.
Azure cache-aside explicitly traces application check, source miss fetch, fill and response, and warns cached/source consistency is not guaranteed.
Azure guidance and cache-aside example distinguish parameterized keys and private data hazards; differing currencies need differing result identity by direct application of those rules.

Cache-aside documents separate write/invalidation and non-guaranteed consistency. The explicit old-read/pause/refill counterexample follows these independent operations and correctly rejects freshness.
Redis eviction confirms maxmemory, LRU, eviction of TTL-bearing keys and noeviction errors. Expiration lifetime does not load a replacement or change a previously fetched source value.
AWS caching article confirms inconsistent per-process copies and shared external values with network/operating dependencies; outage reachability scope follows that topology.

AWS article describes cold/unavailable cache overload and caps/load shedding, independently available local fallback and testing disabled cache. Sharing one in-progress fill reduces repeated source work.

Azure guidance recommends frequent reuse and tolerated staleness; AWS corroborates unique-per-request results produce negligible hits. Measuring source load, response time and hit ratio supports cost-based selection.
